COURT’S OR JUDGES’S ORDERS
CRLR No.476 of 2025
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Siddharth Jain, learned counsel for the 
revisionist. 
2. The present revision is directed against the 
judgment and order dated 27.05.2025 passed by 
learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun 
in Criminal Appeal No.194 of 2023, Ms. Neeta 
Chauhan vs. Shri Mahipal Singh Chauhan, under 
Section 29 of the Protection of Women From 
Domestic Violence Act, 2005 whereby the order 
dated 03.07.2023 passed by learned Additional 
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun in Criminal 
Complaint Case No.2329 of 2011 (Old No.622 of 
2009), dismissing the complaint filed by the 
respondent, was set-aside.
3. It is contended by learned counsel for the 
revisionist that learned appellate court failed to 
appreciate that there is no iota of evidence on 
record to prove that respondent was in 
depression due to revisionist. Further, both sons 
were solely looked after by the revisionist, and 
the respondent never made any effort in their 
upbringing.
4. Issue notice to the respondent, returnable 
within four weeks.
5. Steps to be taken within a week.
6. List on 25.09.2025. 2
7. In the meantime, the execution of the 
judgment and order dated 27.05.2025 passed by 
learned 4th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun 
in Criminal Appeal No.194 of 2023, Smt. Neeta 
Chauhan vs. Shri Mahipal Singh Chauhan, under 
Section 29 of the Protection of Women From 
Domestic Violence Act, 2005 shall remain 
stayed, provided revisionist shall keep on paying 
Rs.15,000/- per month to the respondent on 10th
of every month and shall also pay 25% of the 
arrears within three months from the date of 
passing of this order. 
8. Stay application (IA No.1/2025) stands 
disposed of accordingly.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
06.08.2025 AK

COURT’S OR JUDGE’S ORDERS
CRLR No. 476 of 2025
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Siddhartha Jain, learned 
counsel for the revisionist.
2. Mr. Pushpendra Kumar and Ms. 
Neelima Mishra Joshi, learned counsel for 
the respondent.
3. The revisionist-husband, Mahipal 
Singh Chauhan and the respondent-wife 
Neeta Chauhan are present in Court.
4. On the previous date, learned 
counsel for the respondent apprise to this 
Court that the two sons of the respondent 
are not looking after the respondent￾mother. 
5. Taking into consideration this aspect 
the sons of the parties, were directed to 
join the proceedings, who are serving in 
Army, as a Major and other one is in the 
Bank. Mr. Madhur Chauhan, who is a
Major in Army joined the proceedings 
through V.C. and submits that he and his 
brother are taking all responsibilities to 
look after the mother and will also provide 
accommodation to her at Dehradun and he 
also advised to his mother that since both 
of them are living separately since more 
than 17 years, therefore, don’t compel to
their father to live together. Mr. Madhur 
Chauhan son of the parties undertakes 
that he will search for the accommodation  for his mother.
6. Admittedly, both the revisionist and 
respondent are the senior citizens, living 
separately since last more than 17 years 
and therefore, prima facie, this Court is of 
the view that the marriage in between the 
parties appears to be a dead marriage, in
view of the several decision of the Hon’ble 
Apex Court.
7. List this case on 18.03.2026. By that 
time, their sons search an accommodation 
at Dehradun also to look after her and on 
the next date both the sons shall again 
join the proceedings through V.C.
8. Interim order dated 06.08.2025 shall 
continue. 
 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 
23.02.2026
Nahid

--Revisionist
 Versus
Neeta Chauhan
--Respondent
Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Siddhartha Jain, learned counsel 
for the revisionist/husband.
2. Mr. Pushpendra Kumar and Ms. 
Neelima Mishra Joshi (through Video 
Conferencing), learned counsel for 
respondent/wife.
3. The present matter arises out of 
matrimonial discord between the parties. 
The revisionist and respondent are husband 
and wife respectively.
4. Both the parties are present in person 
before the Court.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the 
respondent/wife would submit that, 
pursuant to the order dated 23.04.2026, the 
respondent/wife has made efforts to identify 
suitable accommodation with a view to 
residing separately and has found a flat, the 
approximate cost whereof is ₹50 lacs.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the 
revisionist would submit that the revisionist 
is not financially capable of bearing the  aforesaid amount and that his maximum 
capacity to make payment towards the 
accommodation of the respondent/wife is 
₹36 lacs. He would further submit that 
certain arrears of maintenance are also 
outstanding against the revisionist and are 
liable to be paid to the respondent/wife.
7. Learned counsel appearing for the 
respondent/wife would submit that the 
balance amount, after taking into 
consideration the amount of ₹36 lacs 
proposed to be paid by the revisionist, may 
be adjusted against and paid from the 
arrears of maintenance payable to the 
respondent/wife. He would further submit 
that the respondent/wife has identified and 
proposed to purchase the aforesaid flat for 
her residential benefit and has placed the 
relevant proposal before the Court. A copy of 
the said proposal has also been handed over 
to learned counsel for the revisionist in 
Court, which has been received by him.
8. On the joint request made by learned 
counsel for the parties, list this case on 
09.10.2026.
9. On the next date of listing, learned 
counsel for the respective parties shall 
apprise the Court of the subsequent 
developments with regard to the proposal 
and the arrangements for the 
accommodation of the respondent/wife.
10. Interim order dated 06.08.2025 to 
continue till the next date of isting.
(Alok Mahra, J.)
 18-09-2026
Mamta
